To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetically engineered mouse model (GEMM) of prostate cancer has provided a unique opportunity to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying initiation, progression, metastasis, and prevention/treatment of this disease.
the genetically engineered mouse models have been widely used to study the initiation, progression and metastasis of prostatic adenocarcinoma.

the genetically engineered mice with prostate-specific expression of human prostate tumor suppressor genes (PTEN and NKX3-1) or oncogenes (c-Myc and Pten) are excellent tools for studying the initiation, progression and metastasis of prostatic intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) and prostate adenocarcinoma (PCa), and for testing novel drugs for PCa prevention and therapy.

the generation and use of genetically engineered mice for prostate cancer research.

the following aspects of prostate cancer: 1) the role of androgen receptor (AR) in prostate carcinogenesis, 2) the role of the androgen receptor in prostate cancer metastasis, and 3) the role of AR in the development of prostate cancer chemoresistance.
the generation and use of genetically engineered mouse models for prostate and other cancers.

the mouse models of prostate cancer are very important tools for prostate cancer research and that the mouse models are very useful to understand the etiologies and pathogenesis of human prostate cancers.
the mouse models for prostate cancers have greatly advanced prostate cancer research and are expected to continue to do so.
the mouse models for prostate cancers are useful for studying the etiology and treatment of prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have established a series of genetically engineered mouse models of prostate cancer, and used them to study the effects of genetic and/or environmental alterations on the initiation, progression and metastasis of prostatic neoplasia, as well as the effects of chemoprevention and chemotherapy agents on prostate cancer.

the development of mouse models for human prostate cancer has provided a valuable platform for testing the effects of genetic alterations and environmental factors on the onset, development, and progression of prostate tumors in vivo.
we developed a series of mouse prostate cancer models and used these models to investigate the roles of androgens, growth factors, and oncogenes in prostate tumorigenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
genetically engineered mouse models are a valuable tool for studying the molecular and biological basis of prostate cancer.

genetic engineering technology is now available to generate a wide range of mouse prostate cancer models that can be used for testing impacts on prostate cancer initiation, progression, metastasis, and treatment.

the genetically engineered mouse models of prostate cancer are powerful tools to dissect the molecular basis of prostate cancer initiation, progression, metastasis and to develop new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of prostate cancer.
